result.reason: A debt-to-equity ratio of nearly 50 is less 'leveraged' and more 'hanging off a cliff by a spreadsheet,' while a profit margin of 3.8% leaves almost no room for error — or optimism. With short float approaching 9% and a P/E of 30 for a company barely keeping the lights on profitably, the market seems to be pricing in hope, which historically has a poor track record as a balance sheet item.
